title: Isoferulic Acid Mitigates Acute Lung Injury Induced by Sepsis Through the Inhibition of JAK2.
authors: Xu, Tong; Xu, Honglin; Zhang, Jiayi; Chen, Guanghong; Han, Xin; Zhang, Guoyong; Hu, Changlei; Pang, Mingjie; Gan, Jian; Hua, Yue; Liu, Bin; Zhou, Yingchun
one_liner_zh: 该文研究异阿魏酸通过抑制JAK2/STAT3通路缓解脓毒症急性肺损伤，涉及分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Sepsis-induced acute lung injury (ALI), among the most severe organ damages, induces irreversible lung injuries and results in a high mortality rate. The occurrence of ALI is highly correlated with the out-of-control inflammatory factors. Therefore, inflammatory inhibition is a crucial measure for treating sepsis-induced ALI. Isoferulic acid (IFA) possesses effective anti-inflammatory effects; however, its role in ALI and its molecular mechanisms remain to be further explored. This work focused on analyzing the possible role of IFA in combating sepsis-induced IFA and exploring the associated mechanisms. CLP mice and LPS-induced RAW264.7 cells were employed as the in vivo and in vitro experimental models. Effects of IFA on inflammation and its mechanisms were assessed using network pharmacology, molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance imaging (SPRi), qRT-PCR, ELISA, immunofluorescence analysis, and Western blot. According to in vivo and in vitro experimental results, IFA down-regulated inflammatory factors TNF-alpha, IL-6, and IL-1beta in CLP mice and LPS-exposed RAW264.7 cells. IFA treatment significantly improved the sepsis-induced inflammation and protected lung function. Furthermore, as revealed by network pharmacology analysis, JAK2 was an important target for the interaction between IFA and ALI. Moreover, molecular docking and SPR results demonstrated a close binding between IFA and JAK2. Further research revealed that IFA suppressed JAK2/STAT3 pathway activation; besides, the therapeutic effect of IFA on ALI was not enhanced by incubation with the JAK2 inhibitor (AG490). Our results offer the preliminary evidence that IFA can restore the impaired function of CLP mice and RAW264.7 cells by alleviating the sepsis-induced inflammation. Additionally, IFA mitigates the sepsis-induced ALI through inhibiting JAK2/STAT3 pathway activation. Therefore, IFA may potentially be used to treat sepsis-induced lung injury.
abstract_zh: 脓毒症诱导的急性肺损伤（ALI）作为最严重的器官损伤之一，会导致不可逆的肺损伤并造成高死亡率。ALI的发生与炎症因子失控高度相关。因此，抑制炎症是治疗脓毒症诱导的ALI的关键措施。异阿魏酸（IFA）具有有效的抗炎作用；然而，其在ALI中的作用及其分子机制仍需进一步探索。本研究旨在分析IFA对抗脓毒症诱导的ALI的潜在作用，并探讨相关机制。采用盲肠结扎穿刺（CLP）小鼠和脂多糖（LPS）诱导的RAW264.7细胞作为体内和体外实验模型。通过网络药理学、分子对接、表面等离子体共振成像（SPRi）、qRT-PCR、ELISA、免疫荧光分析和Western blot评估IFA对炎症的影响及其机制。根据体内和体外实验结果，IFA下调了CLP小鼠和LPS暴露的RAW264.7细胞中炎症因子TNF-α、IL-6和IL-1β的表达。IFA治疗显著改善了脓毒症诱导的炎症并保护了肺功能。此外，网络药理学分析显示，JAK2是IFA与ALI相互作用的重要靶点。进一步研究表明，分子对接和SPR结果证实IFA与JAK2紧密结合。进一步研究发现，IFA抑制了JAK2/STAT3通路的激活；此外，与JAK2抑制剂（AG490）共孵育并未增强IFA对ALI的治疗效果。我们的结果初步证明，IFA通过减轻脓毒症诱导的炎症，能够恢复CLP小鼠和RAW264.7细胞的功能损伤。此外，IFA通过抑制JAK2/STAT3通路激活来缓解脓毒症诱导的ALI。因此，IFA可能具有治疗脓毒症诱导肺损伤的潜力。
